audit_items.proof_trace: Fork digest collision detection is absent in network schedule indexing (line 517). If two different blob parameter configurations produce the same 4-byte digest via XOR (lines 586-589), the byDigest map silently keeps only the first entry, allowing nodes with incompatible blob configs to pass fork digest validation and interoperate.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker crafts node configuration with (BPOEpoch, MaxBlobsPerBlock) values that produce a colliding fork digest through XOR hash truncation. Malicious node passes P2P fork digest validation (rpc_status.go:427) despite having incompatible blob parameters, creating network partition failure where incompatible nodes interoperate.
